title: Etale base change of an algebraic-space infinitesimal pushout
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme and work with algebraic spaces over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A thickening means a representable closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism on underlying spaces; closed immersions are tested after every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion], and underlying spaces have the quotient topology from a surjective etale scheme atlas. Let $i:A\hookrightarrow A^+$ be a thickening, let $a:A\to C$ be affine (representable with affine scheme base changes), and suppose $Q=C\amalg_A A^+$ is a pushout in algebraic spaces over $B$: maps from $Q$ to any algebraic space are exactly compatible maps from $C$ and $A^+$. For a scheme $E$ with a representable etale map $e:E\to Q$, set $C_E=E\times_Q C$, $A_E=E\times_Q A$ and $A_E^+=E\times_Q A^+$. The induced square is a pushout in algebraic spaces over $B$. Explicitly, for every algebraic space $H/B$, restriction induces a bijection $$\operatorname{Mor}_B(E,H)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mor}_B(C_E,H)\times_{\operatorname{Mor}_B(A_E,H)}\operatorname{Mor}_B(A_E^+,H).$$ The spaces $A,C,A^+$ need not be schemes or flat or locally finitely presented over $B$, and the thickening need not have finite order.

proof.text: The pushout existence and recovery lemma identifies the given $Q$ with its constructed pushout, so $C\to Q$ is a thickening. Its base change $C_E\to E$ is a thickening, as is $A_E\to A_E^+$. The map $A_E\to C_E$ is affine: for a scheme $T\to C_E$, its pullback is $T\times_C A\to T$, which is affine by the assumed meaning of affine for $A\to C$. Associativity of fibre products gives $C_E\times_C A=A_E=A_E^+\times_{A^+}A$.

source.place: Tag 07W3, lemma-equivalence-categories-spaces-pushout-flat, part (5) and final counit assertion, specialized to an etale E; Tag 07W0 gives recovery of the two pieces.

proof.text: Form $Z=C_E\amalg_{A_E}A_E^+$. Its projections to $E$ agree on $A_E$, giving a unique $f:Z\to E$ with $e f:Z\to Q$ the projection-induced map. The recovery assertion, applied to the base pushout and this triple, gives $Z\times_Q C\cong C_E$ and $Z\times_Q A^+\cong A_E^+$, with the isomorphisms induced by the two coprojections. Since $C_E\to C$ and $A_E^+\to A^+$ are base changes of $e$, both are chartwise etale. The etale-morphism criterion for pushout triples therefore makes $e f$ chartwise etale.

source.place: Tag 07W3, lemma-equivalence-categories-spaces-pushout-flat, part (5) and final counit assertion, specialized to an etale E; Tag 07W0 gives recovery of the two pieces.

proof.text: Both $Z\to Q$ and $E\to Q$ are chartwise etale, so the permanence lemma for morphisms between etale objects makes $f$ chartwise etale. Moreover $Z\times_E C_E=Z\times_E(E\times_Q C)\cong Z\times_Q C\cong C_E$. The projection in this identification is $f$ restricted over $C_E$, because the recovery isomorphism is induced by the original coprojection $C_E\to Z$. Thus the base change of $f$ to the thickening $C_E\hookrightarrow E$ is an isomorphism. The etale thickening detection lemma shows that $f$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 07W3, lemma-equivalence-categories-spaces-pushout-flat, part (5) and final counit assertion, specialized to an etale E; Tag 07W0 gives recovery of the two pieces.

proof.text: For a compatible pair $u:C_E\to H$, $v:A_E^+\to H$, the pushout property of $Z$ gives a unique $h:Z\to H$. Set $g=h f^{-1}:E\to H$. Since $f$ restricts to the original projections, $g$ restricts to $u,v$. If $g_1,g_2$ restrict to the same pair, then $g_1 f,g_2 f$ have the same restrictions to the two pieces of $Z$, hence are equal; composing with $f^{-1}$ gives $g_1=g_2$. This proves the claimed bijection for every algebraic space $H/B$. No step imposes a finite-order condition.
